notes.claim: BBC Bitesize says that when the V-I graph is a straight line through the origin, current and voltage are proportional.
RMIT says the graph of V versus I for an ohmic conductor is a straight line that must go through the origin.
OpenStax says its plot shows current is proportional to voltage, which is Ohm's law.
OpenStax says that if the line were not straight, the material would not be ohmic and Ohm's law could not be used.
RMIT calls the slope of the V-I graph the resistance, which is constant for an ohmic conductor, so a steeper line means a larger R when voltage is up the side.
BBC Bitesize draws its V-I graph with voltage on the y-axis and current on the x-axis.
notes.contested: Textbooks differ on which axis holds current: Bitesize's explainer puts voltage on y, while another Bitesize guide and OpenStax put current on the vertical axis, so the labels are read every time.
